reasons: Tests cover all-fabricated, mixed and honest citation cases.
The file's own comments explain what each test guards against.

terms.meaning: A test runner for front-end code. It runs the checks and reports which passed.
The plain HTML a component produces when it is drawn without a browser.
A reference to a source that does not exist in the evidence pack.

sections.name: File setup, real
sections.title: Sets up chip tests on real data
sections.what: Loads the real artifacts, builds the evidence lookup, and lists the real evidence ids the tests can use.
sections.why: The header comment says the failure never fires on the golden data, which is why these tests need a fabricated id.
sections.watch_out: The list of real ids comes from the artifacts file, so it changes whenever that file changes.

sections.name: chip
sections.title: Renders the chip to plain text
sections.what: Builds the chip for a list of ids, works out its standing from those ids, and returns the static HTML.
sections.why: Testing the HTML text lets the tests check what a reader would see.
sections.watch_out: Tests read exact wording, so changing a label will break them.

sections.name: a claim whose every citation is fabricated
sections.title: Checks all-fabricated citations
sections.what: Checks that a claim citing only fabricated ids is not shown as grounded, that the warning is present without opening the panel, and that the count reads correctly for one and for two ids.
sections.why: Tests the fix that the component comments describe.
sections.watch_out: The fabricated ids must stay absent from the real data, or these tests stop testing anything.

sections.name: a claim whose citations partly resolve
sections.title: Checks mixed real and fabricated citations
sections.what: Checks that a claim with one real and one fabricated id is still shown as grounded with one item, and still raises the warning for the fabricated one.
sections.why: A real citation must not hide a fabricated one.
sections.watch_out: The test assumes the first real id exists in the data.

sections.name: the honest cases are unchanged
sections.title: Checks honest claims still render correctly
sections.what: Checks that a claim with no citations reads as unsupported with no warning, and that a real citation reads as grounded with no warning.
sections.why: Makes sure the fix does not make honest claims look wrong.

summary: Tests that a claim whose citations do not exist is not shown as grounded, that the missing-citation warning appears without opening the panel, and that honest cases still render correctly.
purpose: Protects the fix that stops fabricated citations from looking like real evidence.
why: The header comment says the failure never happens on the golden data, so only a test with a made-up id can catch it.
how: The file loads the real artifacts and builds the evidence lookup. A helper renders the chip for a list of ids and returns static markup. Tests then check the markup for standing names, the warning text and the counts for one and two fabricated ids, and check mixed and honest cases.
inputs: The generated artifacts file, the evidence lookup, and invented ids such as ones beginning with a fabricated prefix.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the test runner.
risks: The tests depend on real ids from the artifacts file. If the data changes, the first real id may change too.
debug: If a test fails, read the rendered markup it printed and check the standing class and the warning text. Confirm the fabricated ids are still absent from the real data.
